page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. Hardware allocation includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores via two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES. The server type includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and features no GPU acceleration, relying on remote attached storage for disk input and output operations.

Performance metrics reflect strong single-threaded execution capabilities. The D4as_v7 achieves top-tier results in single-core benchmarks, including a stress-ng score of 3781.18, a Geekbench single-core score of 2704.0, and single-threaded gzip compression at 41.21 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-core processing metrics, such as a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 7552.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6334.0, fall within median industry performance brackets. Memory bandwidth provides 455.47 GB/sec for small cached blocks, tapering to 47.24 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 33.71 GB/sec for uncached writes. Network and web benchmarks show static web throughput of 8.92 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 7.94 million operations per second.

The architectural profile offers balanced resource density with high single-core compute capabilities, making it cost-efficient for workloads that do not fully saturate wide core counts. However, because it contains only two physical cores and no integrated local disk, intensive parallel computing and heavy uncached I/O workloads face throughput constraints. The D4as_v7 is primarily aligned with application environments requiring high single-core execution speed alongside balanced memory, including web application servers, microservices, relational database backends, CI/CD compilation tasks, and entry-level small model machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, the instance leverages 2 physical cores with multithreading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and VAES. It contains no onboard local storage, depending entirely on remote block storage, and operates without GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core performance across Geekbench and compression tasks, paired with average multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. Given its elevated per-core clock speed and standard memory density, the D4as_v7 delivers an efficient operational profile for web serving, microservices, CI/CD runners, and relational database hosting.
